Exercise 7. 1. Bread: ten loaves, one pound each; The client buys ten without question. 2. Tomatoes: £20 per kilo; The client protests because they are expensive, the seller explains that the season is over. 3. Turkish coffee: 85 GBP per quarter; the customer wants half a kilo and proposes 160 instead of 170. 4. At the bar: two teas and an anise, 45 GBP; the customer pays with 50 and leave the rest. Exercise 8. a) In an Egyptian grocery store in Milan, ʿAmm Fatḥi. from, to, dōl are demonstrative pronouns: this is fūlThis is what I'm talking about. ṭaʿmiyyaThese are dates. The fūl cost 2,50 The box. The dates come from Siwa and cost 8 Euro a kilo. ʿAmm Fatḥi drops to 7; Luke, at the suggestion of Šarīf, proposes 6; close to 6,50. In all, Luke pays 11,50 EUR (6,50 Of dates and 5 for two boxes of fūl). b) Because next month he leaves for Egypt. She's not new, but she's in a good state. She's two years old. Mīna asks 150 euro (new cost) 300). There's a lock and light. There's no basket. Luke proposes 120 and take it tomorrow; Šarīf He laughs and says he's become Egyptian by now.
